title: Temperature-dependent compatibility study on halide solid-state electrolytes in solid-state batteries
abstract: <jats:p>All-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) have attracted much attention owing to their high safety and energy density compared to conventional organic electrolytes. However, the interfaces between solid-state electrolytes and electrodes retain some knotty problems regarding compatibility. Among the various SSEs investigated in recent years, halide SSEs exhibit relatively good interfacial compatibility. The temperature-dependent interfacial compatibility of halide SSEs in solid-state batteries is investigated by thermal analysis using simultaneous thermogravimetry and differential scanning calorimetry (TG–DSC) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Halide SSEs, including rock-salt-type Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub> and anti-perovskite-type Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>OHCl, show good thermal stability with oxides LiCoO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>, LiMn<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>, and Li<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>Ti<jats:sub>5</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>12</jats:sub> up to 320 °C. Moreover, anti-perovskite-type Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>OHCl shows a chemical reactivity with other battery materials (eg., LiFePO<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>, LiNi<jats:sub>0.8</jats:sub>Co<jats:sub>0.1</jats:sub>Mn<jats:sub>0.1</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>, Si-C, and Li<jats:sub>1.3</jats:sub>Al<jats:sub>0.3</jats:sub>Ti<jats:sub>1.7</jats:sub>(PO<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>)<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>) at 320°C, which reaches the melting point of Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>OHCl. It indicated that Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>OHCl has relatively high chemical reactivity after melting. In contrast, rock-salt-type Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub> shows higher stability and interfacial compatibility. This work delivers insights into the selection of suitable battery materials with good compatibility for ASSLBs.</jats:p>
